skill.name: terraform-skill
skill.description: Provides version-aware guidance for writing, reviewing, testing, and operating Terraform or OpenTofu modules, pipelines, security controls, and remote state.
skill.summary: Diagnose Terraform and OpenTofu risks before generating validated infrastructure changes.
skill.author: antonbabenko

security_audit.summary: The skill has defensive intent and requires reviewed plans, confirmation for destroy operations, and state-secret safeguards. Most static matches are Markdown syntax, Terraform identifiers, placeholders, or labeled examples rather than executable threats. Confirmed risks are an unverified pipe-to-shell installer, its mutable source URL, fragile xargs deletion, an unpinned action, and direct auto-approved apply examples.

remediation.issue: Remote installer and Trivy action are not immutably pinned.
remediation.suggestion: Use a packaged release or pinned commit, verify its checksum or signature, and pin the GitHub Action to a reviewed commit SHA.

remediation.issue: State-locking examples run direct terraform apply -auto-approve.
remediation.suggestion: Create and review a saved plan, require environment approval, then apply that exact artifact with concurrency controls.

remediation.issue: Backup retention parses ls output and sends paths to xargs rm.
remediation.suggestion: Quote variables and use a null-delimited file selection method constrained to the backup directory before deleting files.

content.user_title: Build Safer Terraform and OpenTofu Workflows
content.value_statement: Terraform changes can expose secrets, replace resources, or corrupt shared state. This skill diagnoses those risks and provides version-aware implementation and validation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Diagnoses identity churn, secret exposure, state corruption, CI drift, and provider upgrade risks.
Generates version-aware Terraform and OpenTofu module patterns with typed inputs and stable outputs.
Designs validation pipelines using formatting, validation, testing, security scanning, policy checks, and reviewed plans.
Guides remote backend selection, locking, migration, backup, recovery, and multi-team state isolation.
Provides safe refactoring guidance with moved, import, removed, and version-constrained feature patterns.
Compares native tests, mock providers, Terratest, and policy frameworks by cost and coverage.
limitations: It does not replace provider documentation or verify every provider resource schema.
Cloud operations require configured credentials, installed tools, and user approval.
Examples must be adapted to the selected runtime, provider versions, backend, and environment.
It cannot guarantee a safe apply without reviewing the generated plan and organizational policies.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Shared Module
use_cases.description: Plan address-preserving changes, add migration blocks, and validate that production resources are not replaced.

use_cases.title: Build a Controlled Delivery Pipeline
use_cases.description: Create validation, testing, policy, plan, approval, and exact-plan apply stages for infrastructure changes.

use_cases.title: Recover and Harden Remote State
use_cases.description: Investigate locks or drift, select a recovery path, and document backup and rollback evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Terraform Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Terraform configuration for correctness and safety. State runtime assumptions, identify risks, propose focused changes, and provide validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reusable Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reusable [provider] module for [service]. Target [Terraform or OpenTofu version]. Include typed inputs, stable outputs, tests, security controls, and usage guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Infrastructure Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI/CD workflow for this repository. Separate validation, testing, security, plan, approval, and apply stages. Apply only the reviewed plan artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a State Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this [lock, drift, migration, or corruption] incident. Use the supplied backend details and logs to create evidence-preserving recovery and rollback procedures.

output_examples.input: A module changed from count to for_each and the plan replaces production instances.
output: Risk: resource identity churn can cause unintended replacement.
Recommendation: map old addresses to stable keys with migration blocks.
Validation: review a saved plan and confirm zero unexpected destroys before approval.

output_examples.input: A team wants Terraform to read a database password from a standard variable.
output: Risk: sensitive variables remain in Terraform state even when display is masked.
Recommendation: use supported write-only or ephemeral mechanisms, or keep secret material outside Terraform.
Validation: inspect the plan and state handling without printing the secret.

output_examples.input: A CI job plans again during apply after the pull request plan was approved.
output: Risk: the applied configuration can differ from the reviewed plan.
Recommendation: store the approved plan securely and apply that exact artifact.
Validation: require protected-environment approval and verify artifact provenance.

best_practices: Provide the runtime, exact version, providers, backend, execution path, and environment criticality.
Review saved plans and retain rollback evidence before destructive or state-mutating operations.
Pin runtimes, providers, modules, actions, and lockfiles according to the environment risk.
anti_patterns: Do not apply directly to production without a reviewed plan artifact and approval.
Do not assume sensitive variables keep secret values out of state.
Do not rename resource addresses blindly or use list indexes as durable identity.

faq.question: Does this skill support OpenTofu?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides runtime-specific guidance and asks for the exact Terraform or OpenTofu version before selecting features.

faq.question: Can it write complete Terraform modules?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose module structure, typed inputs, stable outputs, version constraints, examples, tests, and validation steps.

faq.question: Will it run terraform apply automatically?
faq.answer: No. Production changes require a reviewed plan, approval, and an explicit execution decision.

faq.question: How does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It explains state exposure and recommends write-only, ephemeral, managed-secret, or external runtime patterns when supported.

faq.question: Which testing approaches does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers formatting, validation, linting, native tests, mock providers, Terratest, security scanners, and policy checks.

faq.question: Can it recover corrupted Terraform state?
faq.answer: It can develop a cautious recovery procedure from supplied backend details and evidence. Operators must verify backups and authorize mutations.
